question: Do algebraic and operator descriptions of certain conformal theories agree?
idea: The manuscript starts from a simple unitary strongly rational vertex operator algebra and claims it produces a completely rational conformal net. It also matches the corresponding representation categories. These are two precise mathematical encodings of conformal structure; the strong rationality and unitarity assumptions restrict the class covered.
why: Mathematics used to understand physical models, including quantum systems and interacting particles. A theorem concerns a specified model, not every physical situation.

exactClaim: Proves the strongly rational case of the strong-locality conjecture: every simple unitary strongly rational complex vertex operator algebra generates a completely rational conformal net. Its simple modules are unitarizable, and its representation category agrees with the net’s finite-index sectors as a braided unitary tensor category. )
reviewStatus: assistant-authored from source summary; not mathematically reviewed
scope: Family-level introduction based on the pinned catalogue summary. Summarizes manuscript claims; not an independent proof review.
